title: Predict: binary arithmetic
prompt: Trace fixed-width wraparound, carry propagation across a pair of adds, and a signed widening multiply.

predictions.question: What exact decimal value does w20 hold after this code runs?
predictions.explanation: mov w20, -1 writes 0xFFFFFFFF, every one of the 32 bits set. Adding 2 gives 0x100000001, but a w register keeps only the low 32 bits, so the value wraps to 1. Fixed-width addition is always modulo 2^32, and a plain add ignores the carry out of bit 31.
predictions.hint: Only the low 32 bits of the sum survive.

predictions.code:
mov x20, 5
mov x23, 7
mov x21, -1
mov x24, 1
adds x27, x21, x24
adcs x26, x20, x23
predictions.question: What exact decimal value does x26 hold after this code runs?
predictions.explanation: x21 holds 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, so adds leaves 0 in x27 and sets the carry flag. adcs then computes 5 + 7 + 1 and leaves 13 in x26. This is how a 128-bit addition is built from two 64-bit adds.
predictions.hint: adds sets C when the sum carries out of bit 63, and adcs adds that C into its own sum.

predictions.code:
mov w20, 2
mov w21, -5
smull x22, w20, w21
predictions.question: What exact hex value does x22 hold after this code runs? Write all 16 hex digits, starting with 0x.
predictions.explanation: smull sign-extends both 32-bit sources and writes the full 64-bit signed product, so no separate correction step is needed for the negative operand. 2 * -5 is -10, and -10 as a 64-bit two's complement value is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF6.
predictions.hint: Work out -10 as a 64-bit two's complement pattern.
